title: Sprint reflections and private KPI draft
content:
Personal Sprint OKR Draft - Q1 2025

Notes to self: Use this as a running scratchpad for weekly check-ins and small experiments. Keep it private; share only final KRs with manager.

Quick snapshot (2025-03-03):
- P95 latency for local dev traces: 320ms (goal 250ms)
- Cost per 100k tokens (hosted): $7.4 (goal $5.5)
- Canary success rate: 98.7% (target 99.5%)
- Prompt eval pass rate on smoke prompts: 92% (baseline 90%)

Draft OKR (for review with manager):
Objective: Make inference behavior predictable and 20% cheaper for feature X by end of Q1.
Key Results:
- KR1: Reduce average cost per 100k tokens for feature X by 20% vs baseline (current $7.4 -> target $5.9)
- KR2: P95 latency <= 250ms for 90th percentile of requests from EU region
- KR3: Deploy caching policy that yields >= 2x effective cache-hit for repeated prompts
- KR4: Add automated regression alerts (quality) for top 50 prompt families

Weekly check-ins (short):
2025-02-17:
- Ran baseline profiling of model variants (int8 vs bfloat16). int8 saves ~18% cost in microbenchmarks but increases hallucination score on eval-03 set.
- Action: schedule eval sweep with Samir, try temperature adjustments.

2025-02-24:
- Implemented simple prefix-KV cache prototype (local). Observed 1.6x effective throughput for repeating session traces.
- Added two smoke prompts to smoke suite. Need to integrate with CI so we get automatic failures.
- Blocker: infra team needs to enable ephemeral KV store on dev cluster (ticket JIRA-7891).

2025-03-03 (this morning):
- Canary rollout 2: 98.7% success, a small spike in retry rate at 02:15 UTC — likely transient network hiccup. Follow-up: add tracing annotation to isolate retry source.
- Began drafting cost-optimization experiment plan: compare batching window 10ms vs 30ms, test cost/latency tradeoff.

Retrospective notes (end of sprint):
What went well:
- Fast iteration on cache prototype; small wins on throughput.
- Better visibility on canary via new tracing dashboards (Lena helped tune sampling).

What didn't go well:
- Too many half-baked experiments; need clearer pre-mortem for each experiment with success/failure criteria.
- Communication with infra on ephemeral stores was slower than expected; follow-up required.

Action items (owner in parens):
- Convert cache prototype into RFC with perf numbers + safety checklist (Maya)
- Add two more smoke prompts covering edge cases from support tickets (Samir)
- Draft experiment pre-mortem template and get it into team handbook (Maya + Lena)
- Ping infra for ephemeral KV timeline; escalate if no response by 2025-03-07 (Maya)

Open questions / experiments to try next:
- Try quantization-aware finetuning vs straight int8 for hallucination mitigation.
- Evaluate dynamic batching with adaptive window based on current qps.
- Explore cost-savings via model-routing: route low-entropy prompts to smaller model.

Personal reflection / development goals:
- Improve experiment design skills: read "Designing Experiments for ML" over next sprint (block 3x1h/week).
- Pair with SRE on tracing to understand end-to-end latency sources (schedule 1 session).

Misc notes (to self):
- Keep OKR numbers conservative until validated by experiments.
- Keep public notes minimal; this doc is the scratchpad.
- Add final OKR summary to 1:1 notes before manager sync on 2025-03-10.

Related tickets and quick links:
- JIRA-7891 (ephemeral KV) — blocking cache integration
- JIRA-8012 (canary retry spike) — tracing changes
- github.com/redwood/retry-proto/pull/212 — prototype code

End of note.
